page: Microsoft Azure F32ams_v6 is a virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction sets including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, and BF16) and cryptographic extensions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. No dedicated GPUs or local storage drives are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark testing shows high parallel computing and memory performance across multiple synthetic suites. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 21894.0, ranking in the top 10%, alongside a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 98430.89 and a PassMark CPU score of 62593.95. Small-block cached read memory bandwidth reached 4748.97 GB/sec, while uncached large-block write operations achieved 109.68 GB/sec. In application-focused metrics, the server produced 78.25 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and completed PassMark database operations at 29552.73. CPU-based machine learning inference showed 4660.22 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model, though larger 70B models operated at average speeds of 3.36 text generation tokens per second.

From an infrastructure standpoint, the allocation of dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading provides consistent per-thread performance and eliminates core contention. Although categorized under the compute-optimized family, the inclusion of 256.0 GB of memory places its memory allocation at an 8:1 RAM-to-core ratio, which matches memory-intensive operational profiles. A primary operational consideration is the complete absence of local ephemeral storage, requiring workloads to rely on external network-attached volumes for data retention.

The hardware profile makes the F32ams_v6 well suited for memory-intensive computational tasks, enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale software compilation, and parallel data manipulation pipelines that require significant RAM allocations without requiring GPU acceleration.

The system provides 32 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core and 256.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-to-core ratio. The x86_64 processor includes AVX-512 vector extensions and 32 MB of L3 cache. Benchmarks highlight strong compute and memory capabilities, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 21894.0, a PassMark CPU score of 62593.95, and 78.25 million Redis SET operations per second. The server does not bundle local disk storage or GPU hardware. The F32ams_v6 fits memory-heavy compute workloads, software compilation, data transformations, and in-memory databases requiring high RAM capacity per dedicated core.
